newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Earning hopes keep driving MOL up.
newsitem.headline: Earning hopes keep driving MOL up.

text.p: Hungarian oil company MOL's shares have traded substantially above their subscription price in an IPO and analysts say the surge is mainly fueled by talk of strong earnings.
"The main reason (behind the high price) is active rumours on the market of very strong first quarter at MOL," said Spencer Jakab, analyst at CS First Boston in Budapest.
On Friday MOL opened a little weaker but quickly recovered and at 1020 GMT it traded at 3,580 forints, up 120 from Thursday's close.
"Expectations of MOL's first quarter results are very, very positive," added Rudi Voros, analyst at ICE Securities in London.
"Many investors expect a Q1 result equal to the half of MOL's full 1996 earnings," he said.
In 1996 MOL generated an IAS consolidated net income of 22.2 billion forints.

Analysts said MOL's price also reflected the unsatisfied demand in MOL's global offering in which a 12.5 percent stake in MOL was placed to international institutional investors with the joint global coordinators granted an overallotment option of 2.5 percent.
"The most obvious (reason) is that the issue was six times oversubscribed and there are buyers who wanted to get more," Jakab said. "(But) I think that is actually not the main reason."
Another factor was domestic investors' fear that they will be unable to get as many shares as they want in the domestic offer which is to start on Monday.
In the domestic offer a one percent plus an additional three percent is on sale.
The stock was priced at $16.25 or 2,970 forints.
"The (global) offering was six times oversubscribed, meanwhile domestic investors show strong interest in the shares and this pushes MOL's price up," Voros said.
Analysts said the fact that MOL was a major component in the BUX index basket reinforced MOL's rally on the cash market.

"There's an arbitrage opportunity for banks who borrow on the interbank market and buy BUX futures," Jakab said. "Then they buy the underlying BUX components to hedge away the risk, therefore there's a lot of demand for MOL, and OTP and Richter, also."
MOL is expected to release its earnings report following the close of the domestic offer.
